title: Arakhin 15
description: Why a rapist pays for humiliation beyond the fifty sela, the defamer’s hundred and the mishna’s lesson that speech is graver than deed, the spies and the ten trials in the wilderness, and a long chain of teachings on the gravity of malicious speech and its remedy.

a1.he: אִילּוּ בָּאוּ עָלֶיהָ שְׁנַיִם, אֶחָד שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ וְאֶחָד כְּדַרְכָּהּ, יֹאמְרוּ: בָּעַל פְּגוּמָה — חֲמִשִּׁים, בָּעַל שְׁלֵמָה — חֲמִשִּׁים?

a2.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: אִי הָכִי, גַּבֵּי עֶבֶד נָמֵי יֹאמְרוּ: עֶבֶד בָּרִיא — שְׁלֹשִׁים, עֶבֶד מוּכֵּה שְׁחִין — שְׁלֹשִׁים!

a3.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר אַבָּיֵי, אָמַר קְרָא ״תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר עִנָּהּ״, מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא בּוֹשֶׁת וּפְגָם.

a4.he: רָבָא אָמַר, דְּאָמַר קְרָא: ״וְנָתַן הָאִישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵב עִמָּהּ וְגוֹ׳״, הֲנָאַת שְׁכִיבָה חֲמִשִּׁים, מִכְּלָל דְּאִיכָּא מִילְּתָא אַחֲרִיתִי, וּמַאי נִיהוּ? בּוֹשֶׁת וּפְגָם.

a5.he: מַתְנִי׳ בְּמוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר, כֵּיצַד? אֶחָד שֶׁהוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע עַל גְּדוֹלָה שֶׁבַּכְּהוּנָּה וְעַל קְטַנָּה שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל — נוֹתֵן מֵאָה סֶלַע.

a6.he: נִמְצָא הָאוֹמֵר בְּפִיו חָמוּר מִן הָעוֹשֶׂה מַעֲשֶׂה, שֶׁכֵּן מָצִינוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִתְחַתֵּם גְּזַר דִּין עַל אֲבוֹתֵינוּ בַּמִּדְבָּר אֶלָּא עַל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״וַיְנַסּוּ אוֹתִי זֶה עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים וְגוֹ׳״.

a7.he: גְּמָ׳ מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא גָרֵים לַהּ קְטָלָא, דִּכְתִיב: ״וְאִם אֱמֶת הָיָה הַדָּבָר וְגוֹ׳ וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת הַנַּעֲרָה וְגוֹ׳״!

a8.he: אָמַר רָבָא, אָמַר קְרָא: ״כִּי הוֹצִיא שֵׁם רָע״, עַל שֵׁם רַע שֶׁהוֹצִיא.

a9.he: וְכֵן מָצִינוּ שֶׁלֹּא נִתְחַתֵּם גְּזַר דִּין וְכוּ׳. מִמַּאי דִּלְמָא דְּאַכַּתִּי לָא מְלָא סְאָתָן, דְּאָמַר רַב הַמְנוּנָא: אֵין הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא נִפְרָע מִן הָאָדָם עַד שֶׁתִּתְמַלֵּא סְאָתוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״בִּמְלֹאת סִפְקוֹ יֵצֶר לוֹ״.

a10.he: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, אָמַר קְרָא: ״וַיְנַסּוּ אוֹתִי זֶה עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים״, עַל זֶה נִתְחַתֵּם גְּזַר דִּין.

a11.he: תַּנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן פַּרְטָא: בּוֹא וּרְאֵה כַּמָּה גָּדוֹל כֹּחַ שֶׁל לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, מְנָלַן? מִמְּרַגְּלִים; וּמָה הַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע עַל עֵצִים וַאֲבָנִים כָּךְ, הַמּוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע עַל חֲבֵירוֹ עַל אַחַת כַּמָּה וְכַמָּה!

a12.he: מִמַּאי? דִּלְמָא מִשּׁוּם דְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא בַּר פָּפָּא: דָּבָר גָּדוֹל דִּבְּרוּ מְרַגְּלִים בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״כִּי חָזָק הוּא מִמֶּנוּ״, אַל תִּיקְרֵי ״כִּי חָזָק הוּא מִמֶּנוּ״ אֶלָּא ״מִמֶּנּוּ״, כִּבְיָכוֹל, בַּעַל הַבַּיִת אֵין יָכוֹל לְהוֹצִיא כֵּלָיו מִשָּׁם.

a13.he: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבָּה אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ, אָמַר קְרָא: ״וַיָּמוּתוּ הָאֲנָשִׁים מוֹצִאֵי דִבַּת הָאָרֶץ רָעָה״, עַל דִּבַּת הָאָרֶץ שֶׁהוֹצִיאוּ.

a14.he: תַּנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה, עֶשֶׂר נִסְיוֹנוֹת נִיסּוּ אֲבוֹתֵינוּ לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: שְׁנַיִם בַּיָּם, וּשְׁנַיִם בַּמַּיִם, שְׁנַיִם בַּמָּן, שְׁנַיִם בַּשְּׂלָיו, אַחַת בָּעֵגֶל, וְאַחַת בְּמִדְבַּר פָּארָן.

a15.he: שְׁנַיִם בַּיָּם: אַחַת בַּיְּרִידָה וְאַחַת בָּעֲלִיָּיה. בַּיְּרִידָה — דִּכְתִיב ״הַמִבְּלִי אֵין קְבָרִים בְּמִצְרַיִם״.

a16.he: בָּעֲלִיָּיה — כִּדְרַב הוּנָא, דְּאָמַר רַב הוּנָא: יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁבְּאוֹתוֹ הַדּוֹר מִקְּטַנֵּי אֲמָנָה הָיוּ, כִּדְרַבָּה בַּר מָרִי, דְּאָמַר רַבָּה בַּר מָרִי: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״וַיַּמְרוּ עַל יָם בְּיַם סוּף וַיּוֹשִׁיעֵם לְמַעַן שְׁמוֹ״? מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל מַמְרִים בְּאוֹתָהּ שָׁעָה, וְאוֹמְרִים: כְּשֵׁם שֶׁאָנוּ עוֹלִים מִצַּד זֶה כָּךְ מִצְרַיִם עוֹלִים מִצַּד אַחֵר.

a17.he: אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְשַׂר שֶׁל יָם: פְּלוֹט אוֹתָם לַיַּבָּשָׁה! אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, כְּלוּם יֵשׁ עֶבֶד שֶׁנּוֹתֵן לוֹ רַבּוֹ מַתָּנָה וְחוֹזֵר וְנוֹטְלָהּ הֵימֶנּוּ? אָמַר לוֹ: אֲנִי נוֹתֵן לְךָ אֶחָד וּמֶחֱצָה שֶׁבָּהֶם.

a18.he: אָמַר לְפָנָיו: רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם, כְּלוּם יֵשׁ עֶבֶד שֶׁתּוֹבֵעַ אֶת רַבּוֹ? אָמַר לוֹ: נַחַל קִישׁוֹן יִהְיֶה עָרֵב, מִיָּד פְּלָטָן לַיַּבָּשָׁה, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת מִצְרַיִם מֵת עַל וְגוֹ׳״

a19.he: שְׁנַיִם בַּמַּיִם — בְּמָרָה וּבִרְפִידִים. בְּמָרָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיָּבוֹאוּ מָרָתָה וְלֹא יָכְלוּ לִשְׁתּוֹת״, וּכְתִיב: ״וַיָּלֶן הָעָם עַל מֹשֶׁה״.

a20.he: בִּרְפִידִים — דִּכְתִיב: ״וַיַּחֲנוּ בִּרְפִידִים וְאֵין מַיִם לִשְׁתּוֹת״, וּכְתִיב: ״וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם מֹשֶׁה״.

b2.he: שְׁנַיִם בַּשְּׂלָיו [בִּשְׂלָיו] — רִאשׁוֹן וּבִשְׂלָיו שֵׁנִי. בִּשְׂלָיו רִאשׁוֹן — ״בְּשִׁבְתְּכֶם עַל סִיר הַבָּשָׂר״.

b5.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִימְרָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״מַה יִּתֵּן לְךָ וּמַה יֹּסִיף לָךְ לָשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה״? אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לַלָּשׁוֹן: כׇּל אֵבָרָיו שֶׁל אָדָם זְקוּפִים וְאַתָּה מוּטָל, כׇּל אֵבָרָיו שֶׁל אָדָם מִבַּחוּץ וְאַתָּה מִבִּפְנִים, וְלֹא עוֹד אֶלָּא שֶׁהִקַּפְתִּי לְךָ שְׁתֵּי חוֹמוֹת, אַחַת שֶׁל עֶצֶם וְאַחַת שֶׁל בָּשָׂר, ״מַה יִּתֵּן לְךָ וּמַה יֹּסִיף לָךְ לָשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה״?

b6.he: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִימְרָא: כׇּל הַמְסַפֵּר לָשׁוֹן הָרָע כְּאִילּוּ כָּפַר בָּעִיקָּר, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אֲשֶׁר אָמְרוּ לִלְשֹׁנֵנוּ נַגְבִּיר שְׂפָתֵינוּ אִתָּנוּ מִי אָדוֹן לָנוּ״.

b7.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בֶּן זִימְרָא: כׇּל הַמְסַפֵּר לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, נְגָעִים בָּאִים עָלָיו, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מְלׇשְׁנִי בַסֵּתֶר רֵעֵהוּ אוֹתוֹ אַצְמִית״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם: ״לַצְּמִיתֻת״, וּמְתַרְגְּמִינַן: לַחֲלוּטִין.

b8.he: וּתְנַן: אֵין בֵּין מְצוֹרָע מוּסְגָּר לִמְצוֹרָע מוּחְלָט אֶלָּא פְּרִיעָה וּפְרִימָה.

b9.he: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״זֹאת תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת הַמְּצוֹרָע״? זֹאת תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרָתוֹ שֶׁל מוֹצִיא שֵׁם רַע.

b10.he: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״אִם יִשֹּׁךְ הַנָּחָשׁ בְּלֹא לָחַשׁ וְאֵין יִתְרוֹן לְבַעַל הַלָּשׁוֹן״? לֶעָתִיד לָבֹא מִתְקַבְּצוֹת כׇּל הַחַיּוֹת וּבָאוֹת אֵצֶל נָחָשׁ, וְאוֹמְרוֹת: אֲרִי דּוֹרֵס וְאוֹכֵל, זְאֵב טוֹרֵף וְאוֹכֵל, אַתָּה מָה הֲנָאָה יֵשׁ לְךָ? אוֹמֵר לָהֶם: וְכִי מָה יִתְרוֹן לְבַעַל הַלָּשׁוֹן?

b11.he: וְאָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: כׇּל הַמְסַפֵּר לָשׁוֹן הָרָע מַגְדִּיל עֲוֹנוֹת עַד לַשָּׁמַיִם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״שַׁתּוּ בַשָּׁמַיִם פִּיהֶם וּלְשׁוֹנָם תִּהֲלַךְ בָּאָרֶץ״.

b12.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא: כׇּל הַמְסַפֵּר לָשׁוֹן הָרָע רָאוּי לְסוֹקְלוֹ בְּאֶבֶן, כְּתִיב הָכָא ״אוֹתוֹ אַצְמִית״, וּכְתִיב הָתָם ״צָמְתוּ בַבּוֹר חַיָּי וַיַּדּוּ אֶבֶן בִּי״.

b13.he: וְאָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא: כׇּל הַמְסַפֵּר לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, אֹמֵר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: אֵין אֲנִי וְהוּא יְכוֹלִין לָדוּר בָּעוֹלָם, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מְלׇשְׁנִי בַסֵּתֶר רֵעֵהוּ אוֹתוֹ אַצְמִית גְּבַהּ עֵינַיִם וּרְחַב לֵבָב אֹתוֹ לֹא אוּכָל״, אַל תִּיקְרֵי ״אוֹתוֹ לֹא אוּכָל״ אֶלָּא ״אִתּוֹ לֹא אוּכָל״, וְאִיכָּא דְּמַתְנֵי לַהּ עַל גַּסֵּי הָרוּחַ.

b14.he: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר מָר עוּקְבָא: כׇּל הַמְסַפֵּר לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, אוֹמֵר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְגֵיהִנָּם: אֲנִי עָלָיו מִלְּמַעְלָה וְאַתָּה עָלָיו מִלְּמַטָּה נְדוּנֶנּוּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״חִצֵּי גִבּוֹר שְׁנוּנִים עִם גַּחֲלֵי רְתָמִים״, אֵין חֵץ אֶלָּא לָשׁוֹן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״חֵץ שָׁחוּט לְשׁוֹנָם מִרְמָה דִבֵּר״.

b15.he: וְאֵין גִּבּוֹר אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״ה׳ כְּגִבּוֹר יֵצֵא״, גַּחֲלֵי רְתָמִים הַיְינוּ גֵּיהִנָּם.

b16.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מָה תַּקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁל מְסַפֵּרי לָשׁוֹן הָרָע? אִם תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא — יַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״מַרְפֵּא לָשׁוֹן עֵץ חַיִּים״, וְאֵין לָשׁוֹן אֶלָּא לָשׁוֹן הָרָע, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״חֵץ שָׁחוּט לְשׁוֹנָם״, וְאֵין עֵץ אֶלָּא תּוֹרָה, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״עֵץ חַיִּים הִיא לַמַּחֲזִיקִים בָּהּ״, וְאִם עַם הָאָרֶץ הוּא יַשְׁפִּיל דַּעְתּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְסֶלֶף בָּהּ שֶׁבֶר (רוח) [בְּרוּחַ]״.

b17.he: רַבִּי אַחָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא אוֹמֵר: סִיפֵּר אֵין לוֹ תַּקָּנָה, שֶׁכְּבָר כְּרָתוֹ דָּוִד בְּרוּחַ הַקֹּדֶשׁ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״יַכְרֵת ה׳ כׇּל שִׂפְתֵי חֲלָקוֹת לָשׁוֹן מְדַבֶּרֶת גְּדֹלוֹת״. אֶלָּא מָה תַּקָּנָתוֹ שֶׁלֹּא יָבֹא לִידֵי לָשׁוֹן הָרָע? אִם תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא יַעֲסוֹק בַּתּוֹרָה, וְאִם עַם הָאָרֶץ הוּא יַשְׁפִּיל דַּעְתּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְסֶלֶף בָּהּ שֶׁבֶר (רוח) [בְּרוּחַ]״.

b18.he: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל: כׇּל הַמְסַפֵּר לָשׁוֹן הָרָע מַגְדִּיל עֲוֹנוֹת כְּנֶגֶד שָׁלֹשׁ עֲבֵירוֹת, עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וְגִילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת וּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים. כְּתִיב הָכָא ״לָשׁוֹן מְדַבֶּרֶת גְּדוֹלוֹת״, וּכְתִיב בַּעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה ״אָנָּא חָטָא הָעָם הַזֶּה חֲטָאָה גְדֹלָה״.

b19.he: בְּגִילּוּי עֲרָיוֹת כְּתִיב: ״וְאֵיךְ אֶעֱשֶׂה הָרָעָה הַגְּדֹלָה הַזֹּאת״, בִּשְׁפִיכוּת דָּמִים כְּתִיב: ״גָּדוֹל עֲוֹנִי מִנְּשֹׂא״.

b21.he: בְּמַעְרְבָא אָמְרִי: לָשׁוֹן תְּלִיתַאי קָטֵיל תְּלִיתַאי, הוֹרֵג לַמְסַפְּרוֹ, וְלַמְקַבְּלוֹ, וְלָאוֹמְרִין עָלָיו.

b22.he: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא: מַאי דִּכְתִיב ״מָוֶת וְחַיִּים בְּיַד לָשׁוֹן״, וְכִי יֵשׁ יָד לַלָּשׁוֹן? לוֹמַר לָךְ: מָה יָד מְמִיתָה — אַף לָשׁוֹן מְמִיתָה. אִי מָה יָד אֵינָהּ מְמִיתָה אֶלָּא בְּסָמוּךְ לָהּ — אַף לָשׁוֹן אֵינָהּ מְמִיתָה אֶלָּא בְּסָמוּךְ לָהּ? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״חֵץ שָׁחוּט לְשׁוֹנָם״.

b23.he: אִי מָה חֵץ עַד אַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה, אַף לָשׁוֹן עַד אַרְבָּעִים וַחֲמִשִּׁים אַמָּה? תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר: ״שַׁתּוּ בַשָּׁמַיִם פִּיהֶם וּלְשׁוֹנָם תִּהֲלַךְ בָּאָרֶץ״.

b24.he: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דִּכְתִיב ״שַׁתּוּ בַּשָּׁמַיִם פִּיהֶם״, ״חֵץ שָׁחוּט לְשׁוֹנָם״ לְמָה לִי? הָא קָמַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּקָטֵיל כְּחֵץ.

b25.he: וְכִי מֵאַחַר דִּכְתִיב ״חֵץ שָׁחוּט לְשׁוֹנָם״, ״מָוֶת וְחַיִּים בְּיַד לָשׁוֹן״ לְמָה לִי? לְכִדְרָבָא, דְּאָמַר רָבָא: דְּבָעֵי חַיִּים — בְּלִישָּׁנֵיהּ, דְּבָעֵי מִיתָה — בְּלִישָּׁנֵיהּ.

b26.he: הֵיכִי דָּמֵי לִישָּׁנָא בִּישָׁא? רָבָא אָמַר: כְּגוֹן דְּאָמַר ״אִיכָּא נוּרָא בֵּי פְלָנְיָא״. אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: מַאי קָא עָבֵיד? גַּלּוֹיֵי מִילְּתָא בְּעָלְמָא הוּא! אֶלָּא דְּמַפֵּיק בְּלִישָּׁנָא בִּישָׁא, דְּאָמַר: ״הֵיכָא מִשְׁתְּכַח נוּרָא אֶלָּא בֵּי פְלָנְיָא״.

b27.he: אָמַר רַבָּה: כֹּל מִילְּתָא דְּמִיתְאַמְרָא בְּאַפֵּי מָרַהּ, לֵית בַּהּ מִשּׁוּם לִישָּׁנָא בִּישָׁא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כׇּל שֶׁכֵּן חוּצְפָּא וְלִישָּׁנָא בִּישָׁא! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אֲנָא כְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי סְבִירָא לִי, דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי: מִיָּמַי לֹא אָמַרְתִּי דָּבָר וְחָזַרְתִּי לַאֲחוֹרַי. אָמַר

messages.text: Continued from 14b: the mishna ruled that a rapist or seducer pays the fixed fine of fifty sela, and humiliation and degradation besides. Rav Zeira argued that otherwise people would complain that a king’s daughter and a commoner’s daughter would receive the same fifty; Abaye answered that the Torah fixes a slave’s value at thirty whatever his skill. So Rav Zeira offers a different proof:

Had two men engaged in forced intercourse with her, one in an atypical manner, i.e., anal intercourse, leaving her hymen untouched, and one in a typical manner, vaginal intercourse, in which case the second man pays the fine, people will say: Does it make sense that one who engaged in forced intercourse with a tainted woman, who has had anal intercourse, pays fifty sela, and one who engaged in forced intercourse with an untainted virgin also pays fifty sela? Apparently, the fifty sela is the fixed sum of the fine, while the rest of the payment varies on a case-by-case basis.

notes.dh: אילו באו עליה שנים אחד שלא כדרכה
notes.he: תחילה ואח"כ בא עליה זה כדרכה דאכתי הואי בתולה ואית לה קנס [ויאמרו] זה שבעל פגומה דליכא בושת כולי האי יהיב נ' סלעים ואילו בעל בתולה שלימה לא יהיב נמי אלא חמשים אבל השתא גבי בושת איכא חילוק דיהיב דמי בושת לשלימה טפי מפגומה:
notes.en: Had two come upon her, one in an atypical manner: first, and afterward this one came upon her in the typical manner, for she was still a virgin and is owed the fine. [People will say:] this one, who had intercourse with a tainted woman, where there is not so much humiliation, gives fifty sela, while had he had intercourse with a wholly untainted virgin he too would give only fifty. But as it is now, with humiliation there is a distinction, for he pays more for the humiliation of an untainted woman than of a tainted one.

notes.dh: אילו באו עליה שנים אחד כדרכה ואחד שלא כדרכה
notes.he: פרש"י אחד בא עליה תחילה שלא כדרכה ואחד בא עליה כדרכה דאכתי היא בתולה ויש לה קנס ויאמרו זה שבעל פגומה דליכא בושת כולי האי יהיב נ' סלעים ואילו בעל בתולה שלימה דעלמא לא יהיב נמי אלא חמשים ורש"י פירש בפ' בן סורר ומורה (סנהדרין דף עג:) גבי האי דאמר לא משלם עד גמר ביאה ופרש"י שם שהוא מוציא בתולים משמע דבעינן השרת בתולים להתחייב קנס ואינו כן דהא איתא בפ"ק דקדושין (דף ט:) באו עליה י' בני אדם ועדיין היא בתולה פירוש כגון שבאו עליה שלא כדרכה ר' אומר אומר אני הראשון בסקילה וכולהו בחנק וא"ר זירא עלה מודה ר' לענין קנס דכולהו משלמי לפיכך פר"י יאמרו בעל פגומה חמשים זהובים אותו שבעל אחריו כדרכה [בעל שלימה חמשים זהובים אותו שבעל ראשון שלא כדרכה דאז היתה שלימה מיהו לכל הפירושים צ"ל דאותו שבעל שלא כדרכה היה ראשון ובספרים כתוב אותו שבעל כדרכה ולפירוש ר"י ק"ק דהוה מצי למימר באו עליה שנים שלא כדרכה]:
notes.en: Had two come upon her, one in the typical manner and one in an atypical manner: Rashi explains that one first had intercourse with her in an atypical manner and then another had intercourse with her in the typical manner, for she was still a virgin and is owed the fine; and people will say: this one, who had intercourse with a tainted woman, where there is not so much humiliation, gives fifty sela, while one who had intercourse with an ordinary, wholly untainted virgin also gives only fifty. And in chapter Ben Sorer UMoreh (Sanhedrin 73b), on the statement that one does not pay until the completion of intercourse, Rashi explained that this means until he removes her virginity, which implies that removing the signs of virginity is required for liability to the fine. But it is not so, for it is stated in the first chapter of Kiddushin (9b): if ten men had intercourse with her and she is still a virgin, that is, they came upon her in an atypical manner, Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] says: I say that the first is stoned and all the others are strangled; and Rabbi Zeira said about this that Rabbi concedes with regard to the fine that they all pay. Therefore the Ri explains: people will say, one who had intercourse with a tainted woman pays fifty gold coins, namely the one who had intercourse with her afterward in the typical manner; and one who had intercourse with an untainted woman pays fifty gold coins, namely the one who first had intercourse with her in an atypical manner, since at that time she was untainted. In any case, according to all the explanations one must say that the one who had intercourse in an atypical manner was first, yet the books read “the one who had intercourse in the typical manner” [first]. And according to the Ri’s explanation it is somewhat difficult, for [the Gemara] could have said: had two men come upon her in an atypical manner.

notes.dh: אילו באו עליה ב' אחד שלא כדרכה ואחד כדרכה
notes.he: שהראשון שלא בעל כדרכה אינו נותן כלום שלא בעלה ואם זה האחרון [שבעלה] נותן נ' כאילו בעל אשה שלימה שלא בא עליה אדם מעולם יאמרו בעל פגומה כו' אלא ודאי פגומה נותן נ' ותו לא שכבר מבויישת היא ובעל שלימה נותן נ' ובושת:
notes.en: Had two come upon her, one in an atypical manner and one in the typical manner: the first, who did not have intercourse with her in the typical manner, gives nothing, since he did not [take her virginity] [the printed text refers the reader to Tosafot here]. And if this last one, who had intercourse with her, gave fifty as though he had had intercourse with a wholly untainted woman whom no man had ever come upon, people would say: one who has intercourse with a tainted woman [pays fifty, and one who has intercourse with an untainted woman pays fifty]. Rather, certainly for a tainted woman he gives fifty and no more, since she has already been humiliated, and for an untainted woman he gives fifty plus humiliation.

messages.text: @Rav Zeira If so, the same claim can be applied with regard to a slave who is killed by an ox. People will say: Does it make sense that a healthy slave is worth thirty sela and a slave afflicted with boils is also worth thirty sela? Yet the mishna clearly indicates that there is no distinction, as the Torah states a fixed amount.
messages.quote: a tainted woman … pays fifty sela, and … an untainted virgin also pays fifty sela

notes.he: דהוי פגום דומיא דנבעלה שלא כדרכה:
notes.en: Afflicted with boils: he is tainted [i.e., of lesser value], like the woman who had intercourse in an atypical manner.

messages.text: “Then the man that lay with her shall give to the young woman’s father fifty silver shekels, and she shall be his wife, because he tormented her; he may not send her away all his days.” This means that the payment is only for the torment, i.e., the rape. It may be inferred that there are additional payments for humiliation and degradation, beyond payment of the fine.
messages.lead: Rather, Abaye said that the reason the payment of fifty sela does not cover all forms of damage is that the verse states:

verse.he: וְנָתַן הָאִישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵב עִמָּהּ לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָ חֲמִשִּׁים כָּסֶף וְלוֹ־תִהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר עִנָּהּ לֹא־יוּכַל שַׁלְּחָהּ כׇּל־יָמָיו׃ {ס}
verse.en: the man who lay with her shall pay the young woman’s father fifty [shekels of] silver, and she shall be his wife. Because he has violated her, he can never have the right to divorce her.

notes.he: רישיה דקרא ונתן האיש השוכב עמה לאבי הנערה חמשים כסף וגו' (דברים כ״ב:כ״ט) דמשמע הני חמשים כסף יתן בשביל קנס העינוי ומדאיצטריך למכתב הכי מכלל דמיחייב מילי אחרנייתא כגון בושת ופגם דלאו קנסא דעינוי נינהו דבלאו עינוי נמי איכא בושת ופגם היינו נזק ששוה פחות מבתחילה:
notes.en: Because he tormented her: the beginning of the verse is “Then the man that lay with her shall give to the young woman’s father fifty silver shekels” (Deuteronomy 22:29), which implies that these fifty silver shekels he gives as the fine for the torment. And since the verse had to write this, it may be inferred that he is liable for other things, such as humiliation and degradation, which are not the fine for the torment, since even without torment there is humiliation and degradation. [Degradation] is the loss: that she is now worth less than at first.

messages.text: the verse states: “Then the man that lay with her shall give to the young woman’s father fifty silver shekels.” Rava infers from here that payment for the pleasure of lying with the woman is fifty shekel. It may be inferred from here that there are other matters that must be paid by the rapist. And what are they? Compensation for humiliation and degradation.

verse.he: וְנָתַן הָאִישׁ הַשֹּׁכֵב עִמָּהּ לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָ חֲמִשִּׁים כָּסֶף וְלוֹ־תִהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה תַּחַת אֲשֶׁר עִנָּהּ לֹא־יוּכַל שַׁלְּחָהּ כׇּל־יָמָיו׃ {ס}
verse.en: the man who lay with her shall pay the young woman’s father fifty [shekels of] silver, and she shall be his wife. Because he has violated her, he can never have the right to divorce her.

messages.text: Mishna

There are halakhot with regard to a defamer, who falsely claims that his bride was not a virgin, that are lenient and others that are stringent. How so? Both one who defamed a young woman who is the most prominent in the priesthood and one who defamed a young woman who is the lowliest among the Israelites gives payment of one hundred sela, the fine stated in the Torah.

verse.he: וְעָנְשׁוּ אֹתוֹ מֵאָה כֶסֶף וְנָתְנוּ לַאֲבִי הַנַּעֲרָה כִּי הוֹצִיא שֵׁם רָע עַל בְּתוּלַת יִשְׂרָאֵל וְלוֹ־תִהְיֶה לְאִשָּׁה לֹא־יוּכַל לְשַׁלְּחָהּ כׇּל־יָמָיו׃ {ס}
verse.en: and they shall fine him a hundred [shekels of] silver and give it to the young woman’s father; for [that man] has defamed a virgin in Israel. Moreover, she shall remain his wife; he shall never have the right to divorce her.

messages.text: Based on the relative scope of the fines, with the defamer paying twice the sum of the rapist and the seducer, it is apparent that one who utters malicious speech with his mouth is a more severe transgressor than one who performs an action.

notes.he: דנותן מאה סלע והעושה מעשה דאונס בתולה לא יהיב אלא נ':
notes.en: Mishna. It is found that one who utters with his mouth is more severe: for he gives one hundred sela, while one who commits the act of raping a virgin gives only fifty.

notes.he: נמצא האומר בפיו חמור מן העושה מעשה שהאומר בפיו שפלונית פגומה חמור מן הפוגמה בעצמו שזה נותן נ' שקל וזה ק':
notes.en: It is found that one who utters with his mouth is more severe than one who performs an act: for one who says with his mouth that so-and-so is tainted is more severe than one who taints her himself, since this one gives fifty shekels and that one a hundred.

messages.text: And this is corroborated, as we found that the sentence imposed on our ancestors in the wilderness was sealed only due to the malicious speech disseminated by the spies, as it is stated at that time: “All those men that have seen My glory, and My signs, which I wrought in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet they have tried Me these ten times and have not listened to My voice.”

verse.he: כִּי כׇל־הָאֲנָשִׁים הָרֹאִים אֶת־כְּבֹדִי וְאֶת־אֹתֹתַי אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂיתִי בְמִצְרַיִם וּבַמִּדְבָּר וַיְנַסּוּ אֹתִי זֶה עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ בְּקוֹלִי׃
verse.en: none of those involved—who have seen My Presence and the signs that I have performed in Egypt and in the wilderness, and who have tried Me these many times and have disobeyed Me—

notes.he: שלא ליכנס לארץ:
notes.en: The sentence: that they would not enter the Land.

notes.he: גבי מרגלים כתיב דמשמע על זה נתחתם:
notes.en: “These [zeh] ten times”: this is written regarding the spies, and it implies that over this [zeh] the sentence was sealed.

notes.he: [באבותינו וכו'] כדכתיב וינסו אותי זה עשר פעמים וכתיב בתריה אם יראו את הארץ וגו' שעל כל אותן עשר פעמים [שנסו] שלא בטחו בהקב"ה לא נגזרה עליהן גזרה שיפלו במדבר עד שאמרו לשון הרע על הארץ:
notes.en: And so we found [with our ancestors]: as it is written, “yet they have tried Me these ten times,” and right after it, “surely they shall not see the land” (Numbers 14:23). For all those ten times that they tried [Him], not trusting in the Holy One, Blessed be He, the decree that they would fall in the wilderness was not decreed upon them, until they spoke malicious speech about the Land.

messages.text: Gemara

From where is this proven? Perhaps the punishment for the one who defames is more severe because the defamation has the potential to cause his wife’s death. As it is written: “But if this thing be true, that the signs of virginity were not found in the young woman, then they shall bring out the young woman to the door of her father’s house, and the men of her city shall stone her with stones that she die.”
messages.quote: one who utters malicious speech with his mouth is a more severe transgressor than one who performs an action

verse.he: וְאִם־אֱמֶת הָיָה הַדָּבָר הַזֶּה לֹא־נִמְצְאוּ בְתוּלִים לַנַּעֲרָ׃ וְהוֹצִיאוּ אֶת־הַנַּעֲרָ אֶל־פֶּתַח בֵּית־אָבִיהָ וּסְקָלוּהָ אַנְשֵׁי עִירָהּ בָּאֲבָנִים וָמֵתָה כִּי־עָשְׂתָה נְבָלָה בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל לִזְנוֹת בֵּית אָבִיהָ וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרָע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ׃ {ס}
verse.en: But if the charge proves true, the young woman was found not to have been a virgin, then the young woman shall be brought out to the entrance of her father’s house, and the people of her town shall stone her to death; for she did a shameful thing in Israel, committing fornication while under her father’s authority. Thus you will sweep away evil from your midst.

notes.he: דאומר בפיו חמור דמשמע דמשום לשון הרע בלבד קא יהיב להו דלמא משום הכי חמיר האי לשון הרע דגרים לה ביה קטלא:
notes.en: Gemara. From where: [is it proven] that one who utters with his mouth is more severe, which implies that he gives them [the hundred sela] on account of the malicious speech alone? Perhaps this malicious speech is more severe because it can bring about her death.

messages.text: The verse states: “And they shall fine him a hundred shekels of silver, and give them unto the father of the young woman, because he has defamed a virgin of Israel; and she shall be his wife; he may not send her away all his days.” This indicates that he is punished severely for his words, for the defamation, not because she might be put to death.

notes.en: Because he has defamed: on account of the malicious speech alone.

notes.he: וענשו אותו מאה כסף:
notes.en: Because he has defamed: and they fine him one hundred silver shekels.

messages.text: The Holy One, Blessed be He, does not punish a person until his se’a is filled, as it is stated: “In the fullness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits.”

verse.he: בִּמְלֹאות שִׂפְקוֹ יֵצֶר לוֹ כׇּל־יַד עָמֵל תְּבֹאֶנּוּ׃
verse.en:
When he has all he wants, trouble will come;
Misfortunes of all kinds will batter him.

notes.he: כשתמלא סאתו בעונות הרבה אז יצר לו תבא עליו צרה:
notes.en: “In the fullness of his sufficiency he shall be in straits”: when his se’a is filled with many sins, then “he shall be in straits”: trouble will come upon him.

notes.he: כשימלא עונות כמו שמספקות המדה להכיל יצר לו. פורע ממנו:
notes.en: “In the fullness of his sufficiency”: when the sins are full, as things fill up a measure to its capacity, “he shall be in straits”: [God] exacts punishment from him.

messages.text: In other words, one is punished only when he has committed a sufficient number of sins, and the malicious speech of the spies was simply the last of a series of transgressions.

The verse states: “All those men who have seen My glory, and My signs, which I wrought in Egypt and in the wilderness, yet they have tried Me now [zeh] ten times and have not listened to My voice.” The extra word “now [zeh]” teaches that their sentence was sealed for this specific sin, i.e., the malicious speech of the spies.

verse.he: כִּי כׇל־הָאֲנָשִׁים הָרֹאִים אֶת־כְּבֹדִי וְאֶת־אֹתֹתַי אֲשֶׁר־עָשִׂיתִי בְמִצְרַיִם וּבַמִּדְבָּר וַיְנַסּוּ אֹתִי זֶה עֶשֶׂר פְּעָמִים וְלֹא שָׁמְעוּ בְּקוֹלִי׃
verse.en: none of those involved—who have seen My Presence and the signs that I have performed in Egypt and in the wilderness, and who have tried Me these many times and have disobeyed Me—

notes.he: ולאו משום צירוף דאחריני:
notes.en: Over this it was sealed: and not because it combined with the others.

messages.text: Come and see how great the power of malicious speech is. From where do we derive this? From the punishment received by the spies. And if one who defames the wood and rocks of Eretz Yisrael received such a severe punishment, then with regard to one who defames another person, all the more so will he be punished severely.

notes.he: כדכתיב ערים גדולות ובצורות בשמים וארץ אוכלת יושביה היא:
notes.en: Wood and stones: as it is written, “the cities are great and fortified up to heaven” (Deuteronomy 1:28), and “it is a land that eats up its inhabitants” (Numbers 13:32).

messages.text: From where is it known that the punishment of the spies was for malicious speech? Perhaps their punishment was due to the sin explained by Rabbi Ḥanina bar Pappa.

The spies uttered a great statement of blasphemy at that time. As it is written: “But the men that went up with him said: We are not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than us [mimmennu].” Do not read this as “for they are stronger than us [mimmennu]” but rather read it as: For they are stronger than Him [mimmennu], i.e., stronger than God. They were saying, as it were, that the owner, i.e., God, cannot remove His utensils, the inhabitants of Eretz Yisrael, from there.

verse.he: וְהָאֲנָשִׁים אֲשֶׁר־עָלוּ עִמּוֹ אָמְרוּ לֹא נוּכַל לַעֲלוֹת אֶל־הָעָם כִּי־חָזָק הוּא מִמֶּנּוּ׃
verse.en: But the other men who had gone up with him said, “We cannot attack that people, for it is stronger than we.”

notes.he: הקדוש ברוך הוא:
notes.en: The owner: the Holy One, Blessed be He.

notes.he: (לעיל) אל תקרי ממנו אלא ממנו פירוש אל תקרי ממנו רפי אלא ממנו דגש ואינו כן שכל ממנו שבתורה דגושין ואינו מחליף כלל זה בזה וכן מצינו בסיפרי ולא נס ליחה אין כתיב כאן אלא ולא נס ליחה:
notes.en: “Do not read mimmennu but mimmennu”: [some] explain: do not read mimmennu with a soft [nun] but mimmennu with a dagesh. But it is not so, for every mimmennu in the Torah has a dagesh, and there is no difference at all between the one and the other [the same written word means both “than us” and “than him”]. And so we find in the Sifrei on “Nor was his natural force abated [lo nas leḥoh]”: it is not written here [one way], but rather [read it another way] [the printed text gives the same word twice, so the exact contrast is unclear].

notes.he: כלפי מעלה והיינו בעל הבית שבראם:
notes.en: But “than Him”: toward Above, that is, the Owner who created them.

messages.text: Two at the sea: One when the Jews descended into the sea, and one when they ascended from the sea. What is this you have done to us, to take us out of Egypt?”

The Jewish people of that generation, during the Exodus, were of little faith.

What is the meaning of that which is written: “But they were rebellious at the sea, even at the Red Sea. Nevertheless, He saved them for His Name’s sake”? This teaches that the Jews were rebellious at that time, and they said: Just as we are ascending from one side, so too perhaps the Egyptians are ascending from the other side, and we will not be saved.

Our ancestors in Egypt did not perceive Your wonders;
they did not remember Your abundant love,
but rebelled at the sea, at the Sea of Reeds. Yet they were saved, as befits God’s name,
to make known God’s might.

notes.he: יש לתמוה איך היו ישראל באותו הדור כ"כ מקטני אמנה שסברו שכך יעשה הקב"ה נסים למצרים להעבירם מארצם לא"י ואומר ר' בשם אביו רבי שמואל שישראל לא עברו הים לרחבו מצד זה לזה שא"כ היו ממהרים ללכת אל א"י אלא רצועה אחת עברו בים לאורך הים עד שפנו למדבר לצד אחד כי לא היו יכולין ללכת מכל צד אם לא יעברו הים ומצרים היו להם מימינם ומשמאלם לפיכך עברו הים רצועה אחת עד שפנו למדבר מצד אחד וזה כשם שאנו עולין מצד זה ובאנו' למדבר כך מצרים עולין מצד אחר מן המדבר וירדפו אחרינו וישיגו כי סבורים שלא יעברו המצריים בים אלא יבאו מצד אחר ובהכי ניחא הא דכתיב (במדבר לג) ויסעו ממרה וגו' ויחנו על ים סוף ואם עברו רוחב הים עד עבר הים מצד אחר היאך פגעו עוד בים וכי חזרו לאחוריהם אלא ש"מ לאחר שנסעו באורך הים ויצאו כמו כן לאורך הים לדרום מצרים שמצרים כמו כן לרוח דרומית של א"י קרוב לסוף דרומית לצד מערב ונילוס מפסיק בין מצרים ובין א"י והים מצד דרומית של ארץ מצרים ממזרח למערב ונסעו לחוף הים מצפון הים שהוא דרומית של מצרים ואח"כ יצאו לאחר שהלכו כחצי גורן עגולה ויצאו בצד צפוני שלהם שהיא דרומית של ארץ אדום ומזרחית של ארץ מצרים ואח"כ הלכו קצת ימים עד מרה ואח"כ היו עדיין אצל הים וכשהוצרכו ליכנס לא"י לא הוצרכו לעבור הים אלא סיבבו ארץ אדום וארץ מואב שהוא בדרומית של א"י ומזרחית של ארץ מצרים:
notes.en: In brief: Tosafot asks how the Jewish people of that generation could have been of such little faith as to think that the Holy One, Blessed be He, would perform miracles for the Egyptians, bringing them out of their land [across the sea after Israel]. Rabbi [the text gives no further name] answers in the name of his father, Rabbi Shmuel: Israel did not cross the width of the sea from one side to the other, for then they would have hurried on toward Eretz Yisrael. Rather they crossed one strip of the sea lengthwise until they turned toward the wilderness on one side, since they could go no other way without crossing the sea, and the Egyptians were on their right and their left. So “just as we are ascending from this side” into the wilderness, “so too the Egyptians are ascending from another side” of the wilderness and will pursue and overtake us, for they thought the Egyptians would not cross in the sea but would come around another way. This also explains the verse (Numbers 33) “And they journeyed from Marah … and encamped by the Red Sea” [Numbers 33:9–10]: had they crossed the width of the sea to its other shore, how did they meet the sea again? Did they turn back? Rather, it shows that they traveled along the length of the sea and came out likewise along it. Tosafot then traces the route: Egypt lies to the south of Eretz Yisrael toward the west, the Nile separates Egypt from Eretz Yisrael, and the sea runs from east to west south of Egypt; they traveled along the northern shore of the sea, went around like half a round threshing floor, and came out on their northern side, south of Edom and east of Egypt; then they traveled some days to Marah and were still near the sea. And when they had to enter Eretz Yisrael they did not need to cross the sea, but went around the lands of Edom and Moab, south of Eretz Yisrael and east of Egypt. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

notes.he: אע"פ שהבטיחם הקב"ה לא תוסיפו לראותם:
notes.en: So too the Egyptians are ascending from another side: even though the Holy One, Blessed be He, had promised them, “you shall see them again no more” (Exodus 14:13).

messages.text: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to the ministering angel of the sea: Spew out the dead Egyptians onto dry land. The ministering angel said before Him: Master of the Universe, is there a servant whose master gives him a gift and then takes it from him? Since the dead Egyptians were given to me for my fish to eat, how can You retract Your gift?

notes.he: פרנסה לדגים:
notes.en: That his master gives him a gift: food for the fish.

notes.he: כשהן מתים:
notes.en: Spew them out onto dry land: once they are dead.

messages.text: God said to the sea: I will give you one and a half times their number. Although I am taking them back now, later I will give you one and a half times as many people. In the case of the Egyptians it is stated: “Six hundred chosen chariots” (Exodus 14:7), whereas with regard to Sisera, who was defeated at the Kishon Brook, it is written: “Nine hundred chariots of iron” (Judges 4:13).

notes.he: דבפרעה כתיב (שמות י״ד:ז׳) שש מאות רכב ובסיסרא כתיב (שופטים ד׳:ג׳) תשע מאות רכב:
notes.en: One and a half: for regarding Pharaoh it is written “six hundred chariots” (Exodus 14:7), and regarding Sisera it is written “nine hundred chariots” (Judges 4:3).

notes.he: במצרים כתיב (שמות י״ד:ז׳) שש מאות רכב בחור ובסיסרא כתיב (שופטים ד׳:ג׳) תשע מאות רכב ואף על גב דכתיב (שמות י״ד:ז׳) כל רכב מצרים לא קא חשיב אלא השרים של ארץ מצרים היה נתלה אחר השש מאות רכב ומלכים של סיסרא היו תלוים אחר התשע מאות רכב ברזל ואם חיל אנשים בזה יותר מבזה אינו חושש:
notes.en: One and a half of theirs: regarding Egypt it is written “six hundred chosen chariots” (Exodus 14:7), and regarding Sisera it is written “nine hundred chariots” (Judges 4:3). And although it is also written there, “and all the chariots of Egypt” (Exodus 14:7), the Gemara counts only [the six hundred]: the officers of the land of Egypt depended on the six hundred chariots, and the kings of Sisera depended on the nine hundred iron chariots. And if the army of men in one was greater than in the other, it does not concern [the Gemara].

messages.text: The ministering angel said before Him: Master of the Universe, is there a servant who issues a claim against his master for a gift promised to him? Who will be the guarantor? God said to the ministering angel: The Kishon Brook will be a guarantor for Me. Immediately, the sea spewed the Egyptians out onto the land, and the Jewish people came and saw that they were dead. As it is written: “And Israel saw the Egyptians dead upon the seashore.”

verse.he: וַיּוֹשַׁע יְהֹוָה בַּיּוֹם הַהוּא אֶת־יִשְׂרָאֵל מִיַּד מִצְרָיִם וַיַּרְא יִשְׂרָאֵל אֶת־מִצְרַיִם מֵת עַל־שְׂפַת הַיָּם׃
verse.en: Thus GOD delivered Israel that day from the Egyptians. Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the shore of the sea.

messages.text: Two with water: One in Mara and one in Rephidim. The Jewish people tested God in Mara as it is written: “And when they came to Mara, they could not drink of the waters of Mara, for they were bitter. Therefore the name of it was called Mara,” as Mara means bitter.

verse.he: וַיָּבֹאוּ מָרָתָה וְלֹא יָכְלוּ לִשְׁתֹּת מַיִם מִמָּרָה כִּי מָרִים הֵם עַל־כֵּן קָרָא־שְׁמָהּ מָרָה׃
verse.en: They came to Marah, but they could not drink the water of Marah because it was bitter; that is why it was named Marah.

notes.he: וקשיא לי מ"ט לא קא חשיב מים במדבר צין:
notes.en: [Two with water:] at Mara and at Rephidim. And it is difficult for me: why does it not count the water in the wilderness of Zin [Numbers 20]?

messages.text: And it is written: “And the people murmured against Moses, saying: What shall we drink?”

verse.he: וַיִּלֹּנוּ הָעָם עַל־מֹשֶׁה לֵּאמֹר מַה־נִּשְׁתֶּה׃
verse.en: And the people grumbled against Moses, saying, “What shall we drink?”

messages.text: The Jewish people also tested God in Rephidim, as it is written: “And all the congregation of the children of Israel journeyed from the wilderness of Sin, by their stages, according to the commandment of the Lord, and encamped in Rephidim; and there was no water for the people to drink.”

verse.he: וַיִּסְעוּ כׇּל־עֲדַת בְּנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵל מִמִּדְבַּר־סִין לְמַסְעֵיהֶם עַל־פִּי יְהֹוָה וַיַּחֲנוּ בִּרְפִידִים וְאֵין מַיִם לִשְׁתֹּת הָעָם׃
verse.en: From the wilderness of Sin the whole Israelite community continued by stages as GOD would command. They encamped at Rephidim, and there was no water for the people to drink.

messages.text: And it is written: “And the people fought with Moses, and said: Give us water that we may drink. And Moses said to them: Why do you fight with me? Why do you test the Lord?”

verse.he: וַיָּרֶב הָעָם עִם־מֹשֶׁה וַיֹּאמְרוּ תְּנוּ־לָנוּ מַיִם וְנִשְׁתֶּה וַיֹּאמֶר לָהֶם מֹשֶׁה מַה־תְּרִיבוּן עִמָּדִי מַה־תְּנַסּוּן אֶת־יְהֹוָה׃
verse.en: The people quarreled with Moses. “Give us water to drink,” they said; and Moses replied to them, “Why do you quarrel with me? Why do you try GOD?”

messages.text: Two with manna, as it is written:

“Do not go out,” as indicated in the verse: “And Moses said: Eat that today; for today is a Sabbath for the Lord; today you will not find it in the field.” But nevertheless there were people who went out to look for manna, as it is written: “And it came to pass on the seventh day that some of the people went out to gather, and they found none.”

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אִכְלֻהוּ הַיּוֹם כִּי־שַׁבָּת הַיּוֹם לַיהֹוָה הַיּוֹם לֹא תִמְצָאֻהוּ בַּשָּׂדֶה׃ שֵׁשֶׁת יָמִים תִּלְקְטֻהוּ וּבַיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי שַׁבָּת לֹא יִהְיֶה־בּוֹ׃ וַיְהִי בַּיּוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי יָצְאוּ מִן־הָעָם לִלְקֹט וְלֹא מָצָאוּ׃ {ס}
verse.en: Then Moses said, “Eat it today, for today is a sabbath of GOD; you will not find it today on the plain. Six days you shall gather it; on the seventh day, the sabbath, there will be none.” Yet some of the people went out on the seventh day to gather, but they found nothing.

notes.he: בשבת ללקוט:
notes.en: Do not go out: on Shabbat, to gather.

messages.text: The verse also states: “And Moses said to them: Let no man leave any of it until the morning,” and there were people who left it until morning, as it states: “But they did not listen to Moses; and some of them left of it until the morning, and it bred worms, and rotted; and Moses was angry with them.”

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר מֹשֶׁה אֲלֵהֶם אִישׁ אַל־יוֹתֵר מִמֶּנּוּ עַד־בֹּקֶר׃ וְלֹא־שָׁמְעוּ אֶל־מֹשֶׁה וַיּוֹתִרוּ אֲנָשִׁים מִמֶּנּוּ עַד־בֹּקֶר וַיָּרֻם תּוֹלָעִים וַיִּבְאַשׁ וַיִּקְצֹף עֲלֵהֶם מֹשֶׁה׃
verse.en: And Moses said to them, “Let no one leave any of it over until morning.” But they paid no attention to Moses; some of them left of it until morning, and it became infested with maggots and stank. And Moses was angry with them.

messages.text: There were two trials relating to the quail, one was on the first occasion when the quail appeared, and the other on the second occasion the quail appeared.

The trial of the first quail is described in the verse: “And the children of Israel said to them: Would that we had died by the hand of the Lord in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the meat pots, when we ate bread to the full; for you have brought us into this wilderness, to kill this whole assembly with hunger.” Immediately afterward the quail arrived, as the verse states: “And it came to pass in the evening, that the quail came up, and covered the camp; and in the morning there was a layer of dew round about the camp” (Exodus 16:13).

verse.he: וַיֹּאמְרוּ אֲלֵהֶם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מִי־יִתֵּן מוּתֵנוּ בְיַד־יְהֹוָה בְּאֶרֶץ מִצְרַיִם בְּשִׁבְתֵּנוּ עַל־סִיר הַבָּשָׂר בְּאׇכְלֵנוּ לֶחֶם לָשֹׂבַע כִּי־הוֹצֵאתֶם אֹתָנוּ אֶל־הַמִּדְבָּר הַזֶּה לְהָמִית אֶת־כׇּל־הַקָּהָל הַזֶּה בָּרָעָב׃ {ס}
verse.en: The Israelites said to them, “If only we had died by GOD’s hand in the land of Egypt, when we sat by the fleshpots, when we ate our fill of bread! For you have brought us out into this wilderness to starve this whole congregation to death.”

notes.he: כשהתחיל המן לירד היה שליו יורד עמו כדכתיב (שמות טז) ויהי בערב ותעל השליו וגו' ובבקר היתה שכבת הטל וגו' ולאחר זמן מרובה התאוו יותר:
notes.en: With the first quail: when the manna began to fall, the quail came down with it, as it is written (Exodus 16:13): “And it came to pass in the evening, that the quail came up … and in the morning there was a layer of dew.” And after a long time they desired more.

notes.he: פרש"י התאוו יותר משמע שלא פסק להם השליו רש"י והר"ר יוסף קרא. פירש שפסק להם השליו ראשון והאספסוף אשר בקרבו התאוו תאוה לפי שלא היה להם שליו וירד להם שליו שני:
notes.en: They desired a desire: Rashi explains “they desired more,” implying that the quail had not stopped coming for them. [The printed text then names] Rashi and Rabbi Yosef Kara: [one] explained that the first quail had stopped, and “the mixed multitude that was among them desired a desire” because they had no quail, and then the second quail came down for them.

messages.text: The second trial of the quail is described in the verse: “And the mixed multitude that was among them desired; and the children of Israel also wept on their part, and said: Would that we were given meat to eat.” Later the verse states: “And there went forth a wind from the Lord, and brought across quails from the sea and let them fall by the camp, about a day’s journey on this side and a day’s journey on the other side, round about the camp, and about two cubits above the face of the earth” (Numbers 11:31).

verse.he: וְהָאסַפְסֻף אֲשֶׁר בְּקִרְבּוֹ הִתְאַוּוּ תַּאֲוָה וַיָּשֻׁבוּ וַיִּבְכּוּ גַּם בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל וַיֹּאמְרוּ מִי יַאֲכִלֵנוּ בָּשָׂר׃
verse.en: The riffraff in their midst felt a gluttonous craving; and then the Israelites wept and said, “If only we had meat to eat!

messages.text: The trial of the golden calf is as it is described in the Torah (Exodus, chapter 32), and the trial in the wilderness of Paran is as it is described in the Torah (Numbers, chapter 13).

notes.he: מעשה מרגלים:
notes.en: In the wilderness of Paran: the episode of the spies.

notes.he: במדבר פארן כדאיתיה בשעת ביאת מרגלים:
notes.en: In the wilderness of Paran: as it is [described], at the time the spies came.

messages.text: What is the meaning of that which is written: “What shall be given to you, and what more shall be done for you, you deceitful tongue”? The Holy One, Blessed be He said to the tongue: All the other limbs of a person are upright, but you are lying horizontally. All the other limbs of a person are external, but you are internal. And moreover, I have surrounded you with two walls, one of bone, i.e., the teeth, and one of flesh, the lips. What shall be given to you and what more shall be done for you, to prevent you from speaking in a deceitful manner, tongue?
messages.lead: § Returning to the topic of malicious speech:

verse.he: מַה־יִּתֵּן לְךָ וּמַה־יֹּסִיף לָךְ לָשׁוֹן רְמִיָּה׃
verse.en:
What can you profit,
what can you gain,
O deceitful tongue?

notes.he: שינים:
notes.en: Of bone: the teeth.

notes.dh: מה יתן לך ומה יוסיף לך
notes.he: עוד הקדוש ברוך הוא שמירה שלא תספר לשון הרע:
notes.en: “What shall He give you, and what more shall He add for you”: [what more can] the Holy One, Blessed be He, [add as] a guard, so that you will not tell malicious speech?

notes.he: [מה יתן לך וכו' כלומר מה יכולת לך להנאתך ולא עשיתי מפני מה את רמיה]:
notes.en: [“What shall be given to you” etc.: that is, what could I have done for you, for your own good, that I have not done? Why, then, are you deceitful?]

notes.dh: אחת של עצם ואחת של בשר
notes.he: שיניים ושפתים:
notes.en: One of bone and one of flesh: teeth and lips.

messages.text: Anyone who speaks malicious speech is considered as though he denied the fundamental belief in God. As it is stated: “Who have said: We will make our tongue mighty; our lips are with us: Who is lord over us?”

verse.he: אֲשֶׁר אָמְרוּ ׀ לִלְשֹׁנֵנוּ נַגְבִּיר שְׂפָתֵינוּ אִתָּנוּ מִי אָדוֹן לָנוּ׃
verse.en:
They say, “By our tongues we shall prevail;
with lips such as ours, who can be our master?”

notes.he: האומרים ללשוננו נגביר כמי שאומר מי אדון לנו דכופרים בעיקר:
notes.en: “Who have said: We will make our tongue mighty”: they are like one who says “Who is lord over us?”, for they deny the fundamental [belief in God].

messages.text: Anyone who speaks malicious speech will be afflicted by leprous marks coming upon him, as it is stated: “Whoever defames his neighbor in secret, I will destroy him [atzmit]; whoever is haughty of eye and proud of heart, I will not suffer him.”

verse.he: (מלושני) [מְלׇשְׁנִי] בַסֵּתֶר ׀ רֵעֵהוּ אוֹתוֹ אַצְמִית גְּבַהּ־עֵינַיִם וּרְחַב לֵבָב אֹתוֹ לֹא אוּכָל׃
verse.en:
One who slanders a friend in secret I will destroy;
I cannot endure anyone haughty and proud.

messages.text: And it is written there: “And the land shall not be sold in perpetuity [letzmitut]; for the land is Mine; for you are strangers and settlers with Me.” And we translate this term letzmitut as laḥalutin, in perpetuity or confirmed.

verse.he: וְהָאָרֶץ לֹא תִמָּכֵר לִצְמִתֻת כִּי־לִי הָאָרֶץ כִּי־גֵרִים וְתוֹשָׁבִים אַתֶּם עִמָּדִי׃
verse.en: But the land must not be sold beyond reclaim, for the land is Mine; you are but strangers resident with Me.

messages.text: The difference between a quarantined leper, i.e., one examined by a priest who found his symptoms inconclusive, and who must therefore remain in isolation for a period of up to two weeks to see if conclusive symptoms develop, and a confirmed [muḥlat] leper, one whose symptoms were conclusive and the priest declared him a definite leper, is only with regard to letting the hair on one’s head grow wild and rending one’s garments.

A confirmed leper is obligated to let the hair on his head grow wild and rend his garments; a quarantined leper is not. The similarity in the terms teaches that one who speaks malicious speech will be afflicted with leprous marks.

notes.he: אלמא אצמית דמתרגם לשון חליטה היינו צרעת:
notes.en: And a confirmed [muḥlat] leper: evidently atzmit, which the Targum renders with the language of ḥalita [confirmation], refers to leprosy.

messages.text: What is the meaning of that which is written: “This shall be the law of the leper [metzora] in the day of his cleansing: He shall be brought to the priest”? This means that this shall be the law of a defamer [motzi shem ra].

verse.he: זֹאת תִּהְיֶה תּוֹרַת הַמְּצֹרָע בְּיוֹם טׇהֳרָתוֹ וְהוּבָא אֶל־הַכֹּהֵן׃
verse.en:
This shall be the ritual for a leper, a person afflicted with ṣaraʻath; see note at 13.3. at the time of being purified.
When it has been reported to the priest,

notes.dh: ואמר ריש לקיש מאי דכתיב זאת תהיה תורת המצורע תורת מוציא שם רע
notes.he: אמר גרסינן ולא גרסי' ואמר דהא ריש לקיש לא אמר כלל לעיל:
notes.en: Reish Lakish says: what is the meaning of that which is written, “This shall be the law of the leper [metzora]”? The law of a defamer [motzi shem ra]: we read “Reish Lakish says,” and not “And Reish Lakish says,” since Reish Lakish said nothing above [in this passage].

messages.text: What is the meaning of that which is written: “If the serpent bites before it is charmed, then what advantage is there to the master of the tongue”? What is the connection between the serpent and the master of the tongue?

verse.he: אִם־יִשֹּׁךְ הַנָּחָשׁ בְּלוֹא־לָחַשׁ וְאֵין יִתְרוֹן לְבַעַל הַלָּשׁוֹן׃
verse.en: If the snake bites because no spell was uttered, no advantage is gained by the trained charmer.

notes.he: היינו שנושך הנחש במקום שאין שם חבר שילחשו. ואית דמפרשי אם ישוך הנחש בלא לחש כלומר אי אפשר לו לישוך אלא א"כ לחשו לו מן השמים שצוו לו:
notes.en: “If the serpent bites without charming”: that is, the serpent bites in a place where there is no charmer to charm it. And some explain “If the serpent bites without a whisper”: that is, it cannot bite unless it was whispered to from Heaven, commanding it.

messages.text: In the future, all the animals will gather and come to the serpent and will say to it: A lion tramples with its paws to kill its prey and eats; a wolf tears with its teeth to kill its prey and eats. But you, what benefit do you have when you bite, as you cannot eat every animal that you kill? The serpent will say to them: And what is the benefit to the master of the tongue that speaks malicious speech?

notes.he: דמה הנאה לבעל הלשון הרע שאומר לשון הרע הרי מצא לו חבר:
notes.en: “There is no advantage to the master of the tongue”: for what benefit does the master of the malicious tongue have in speaking malicious speech? So [the serpent] has found itself a companion.

messages.text: Anyone who speaks malicious speech increases his sins until the heavens, as it is stated: “They have set their mouth against the heavens, and their tongue walks through the earth.” In other words, while his tongue walks on the earth, his sin reaches the heavens.

verse.he: שַׁתּוּ בַשָּׁמַיִם פִּיהֶם וּלְשׁוֹנָם תִּהֲלַךְ בָּאָרֶץ׃
verse.en:
They set their mouths against heaven,
and their tongues range over the earth.

messages.text: Anyone who speaks malicious speech, it is appropriate to stone him with stones. It is written here: “Whoever defames his neighbor in secret, I will destroy him [atzmit],” and it is written there: “They have destroyed [tzamtu] my life in the dungeon, and have cast stones upon me.”

verse.he: צָמְתוּ בַבּוֹר חַיָּי וַיַּדּוּ־אֶבֶן בִּי׃ {ס}
verse.en:
They have ended my life in a pit
And cast stones at me.

notes.he: היא אבן שהניחו על פי הבור כשהשליכו לדניאל לתוכו:
notes.en: “And have cast stones upon me”: this is the stone they placed over the mouth of the pit when they cast Daniel into it.

messages.text: With regard to anyone who speaks malicious speech, the Holy One, Blessed be He says about him: He and I cannot dwell together in the world. As it is stated in the verse: “Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret, I will destroy him; whoever is haughty of eye and proud of heart, I will not suffer him.” Do not read the phrase as: “I will not suffer him [oto],” but as: With him [ito] I cannot bear to dwell. God is saying that He cannot bear having this person in the world with Him.

verse.he: (מלושני) [מְלׇשְׁנִי] בַסֵּתֶר ׀ רֵעֵהוּ אוֹתוֹ אַצְמִית גְּבַהּ־עֵינַיִם וּרְחַב לֵבָב אֹתוֹ לֹא אוּכָל׃
verse.en:
One who slanders a friend in secret I will destroy;
I cannot endure anyone haughty and proud.

notes.he: בהאי קרא לעיל כתיב מלשני בסתר רעהו:
notes.en: “Him [oto] I will not suffer”: in this same verse it is written above, “Whoever slanders his neighbor in secret.”

messages.text: And there are those who teach this notion of God’s not being able to tolerate a certain type of person in reference to the arrogant, i.e., they apply it to the last part of the verse: Proud of heart.

notes.he: להא דרב חסדא דבהאי קרא דאותו לא אוכל כתיב נמי גבה עינים:
notes.en: Concerning the arrogant: [some teach] this statement of Rav Ḥisda about them, for in this verse of “him I will not suffer” it is also written “haughty of eye.”

messages.text: With regard to anyone who speaks malicious speech, the Holy One Blessed be He says about him to Gehenna: I will be on him from above, and you will be on him from below, and together we will judge him and punish him. As it is stated: “Sharp arrows of the mighty, with coals of broom.”

verse.he: חִצֵּי גִבּוֹר שְׁנוּנִים עִם גַּחֲלֵי רְתָמִים׃
verse.en:
A warrior’s sharp arrows,
with hot coals of broom-wood.

notes.he: נדוננו גרסי':
notes.en: We read nedunenu [“we will judge him”].

notes.he: ביחד:
notes.en: Nedonu: together.

messages.text: And the word “arrow” means nothing other than the tongue, as it is stated: “Their tongue is a sharpened arrow; it speaks deceit. One speaks peaceably to his neighbor with his mouth, but in his heart he lies in wait for him.”

verse.he: חֵץ (שוחט) [שָׁחוּט] לְשׁוֹנָם מִרְמָה דִבֵּר בְּפִיו שָׁלוֹם אֶת־רֵעֵהוּ יְדַבֵּר וּבְקִרְבּוֹ יָשִׂים אׇרְבּוֹ׃
verse.en:
Their tongue is a sharpened arrow,
They use their mouths to deceive.
They speak to their fellows in friendship,
But lay an ambush for them in their hearts.

messages.text: And the word “mighty” in Psalms 120:4 means nothing other than the Holy One, Blessed be He, as it is stated: “The Lord will go forth as a mighty man, He will stir up jealousy like a man of war; He will cry; He will shout aloud, He will prove Himself mighty against His enemies.” And as for the coals of the broom tree [gaḥalei retamim] that burn for a long time, this is an allusion to Gehenna.

verse.he: יְהֹוָה כַּגִּבּוֹר יֵצֵא כְּאִישׁ מִלְחָמוֹת יָעִיר קִנְאָה יָרִיעַ אַף־יַצְרִיחַ עַל־אֹיְבָיו יִתְגַּבָּר׃ {ס}
verse.en:
GOD goes forth like a warrior,
Whipping up rage like a fighter—
Yelling, roaring aloud,
Then charging upon the enemy.

messages.text: What is the remedy for those who speak malicious speech? If he is a Torah scholar, let him study Torah, as it is stated: “A soothing tongue is a tree of life, but its perverseness is a broken spirit.”

verse.he: מַרְפֵּא לָשׁוֹן עֵץ חַיִּים וְסֶלֶף בָּהּ שֶׁבֶר בְּרוּחַ׃
verse.en:
A healing tongue is a tree of life,
But a devious one makes for a broken spirit.

messages.text: And the word “tongue” means nothing other than malicious speech, as it is stated: “Their tongue is a sharpened arrow; it speaks deceit.”

verse.he: חֵץ (שוחט) [שָׁחוּט] לְשׁוֹנָם מִרְמָה דִבֵּר בְּפִיו שָׁלוֹם אֶת־רֵעֵהוּ יְדַבֵּר וּבְקִרְבּוֹ יָשִׂים אׇרְבּוֹ׃
verse.en:
Their tongue is a sharpened arrow,
They use their mouths to deceive.
They speak to their fellows in friendship,
But lay an ambush for them in their hearts.

messages.text: And the word “tree” means nothing other than Torah, as it is stated: “It is a tree of life to them that lay hold of it.”

verse.he: עֵץ־חַיִּים הִיא לַמַּחֲזִיקִים בָּהּ וְתֹמְכֶיהָ מְאֻשָּׁר׃ {פ}
verse.en:
She is a tree of life to those who grasp her,
And whoever holds on to her is happy.

messages.text: And if he is an ignoramus, let him humble his mind, as it is stated: “Its perverseness is a broken spirit.” In other words, one who perverts his tongue with malicious speech should remedy his behavior by cultivating a broken and humble spirit.

verse.he: מַרְפֵּא לָשׁוֹן עֵץ חַיִּים וְסֶלֶף בָּהּ שֶׁבֶר בְּרוּחַ׃
verse.en:
A healing tongue is a tree of life,
But a devious one makes for a broken spirit.

notes.he: מי שסולף בה וחפץ לסלקה שלא תהא בו עוד ישבור רוחו:
notes.en: “And perverseness in it [vesalef bah]”: one who perverts [his tongue] with it and wishes to remove it, so that it is no longer in him, should break his spirit.

notes.he: מי שסילף לשונו בה:
notes.en: “And perverseness in it [vesalef bah]”: one who has perverted his tongue with it.

notes.he: ישפיל דעתו:
notes.en: “A broken spirit”: let him humble his mind.

messages.text: If one has already spoken malicious speech, he has no remedy, as King David, inspired by Divine Spirit, has already cut him off with the punishment of karet, as it is stated: “May the Lord cut off [yakhret] all flattering lips, the tongue that speaks great things.”

verse.he: יַכְרֵת יְהֹוָה כׇּל־שִׂפְתֵי חֲלָקוֹת לָשׁוֹן מְדַבֶּרֶת גְּדֹלוֹת׃
verse.en:
May GOD cut off all flattering lips,
every tongue that speaks arrogance.

notes.he: לשון כרת:
notes.en: Karetu: the language of karet [being cut off].

messages.text: Rather, what is his remedy beforehand, so that he does not come to speak malicious speech? If he is a Torah scholar, let him study Torah; and if he is an ignoramus let him humble his mind, as it is stated: “A soothing tongue is a tree of life, but its perverseness is a broken spirit.” One who is humble will not come to speak badly about another.

verse.he: מַרְפֵּא לָשׁוֹן עֵץ חַיִּים וְסֶלֶף בָּהּ שֶׁבֶר בְּרוּחַ׃
verse.en:
A healing tongue is a tree of life,
But a devious one makes for a broken spirit.

messages.text: Anyone who speaks malicious speech increases his sins to the degree that they correspond to the three cardinal transgressions: Idol worship, and forbidden sexual relations, and bloodshed.
This can be derived from a verbal analogy based on the word “great.” It is written here: “May the Lord cut off all flattering lips, the tongue that speaks great things.”

verse.he: יַכְרֵת יְהֹוָה כׇּל־שִׂפְתֵי חֲלָקוֹת לָשׁוֹן מְדַבֶּרֶת גְּדֹלוֹת׃
verse.en:
May GOD cut off all flattering lips,
every tongue that speaks arrogance.

messages.text: And it is written with regard to idol worship: “And Moses returned to the Lord, and said: Oh, this people have sinned a great sin, and have made for themselves a god of gold.”

verse.he: וַיָּשׇׁב מֹשֶׁה אֶל־יְהֹוָה וַיֹּאמַר אָנָּא חָטָא הָעָם הַזֶּה חֲטָאָה גְדֹלָה וַיַּעֲשׂוּ לָהֶם אֱלֹהֵי זָהָב׃
verse.en: Moses went back to GOD and said, “Alas, this people is guilty of a great sin in making for themselves a god of gold.

messages.text: With regard to forbidden sexual relations it is written that when Potiphar’s wife attempted to seduce Joseph he responded: “How can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?”

verse.he: אֵינֶנּוּ גָדוֹל בַּבַּיִת הַזֶּה מִמֶּנִּי וְלֹא־חָשַׂךְ מִמֶּנִּי מְאוּמָה כִּי אִם־אוֹתָךְ בַּאֲשֶׁר אַתְּ־אִשְׁתּוֹ וְאֵיךְ אֶעֱשֶׂה הָרָעָה הַגְּדֹלָה הַזֹּאת וְחָטָאתִי לֵאלֹהִים׃
verse.en: He wields no more authority in this house than I, and he has withheld nothing from me except yourself, since you are his wife. How then could I do this most wicked thing, and sin before God?”

messages.text: With regard to bloodshed it is written, after Cain murdered his brother: “And Cain said to the Lord: My punishment is greater than I can bear.”

verse.he: וַיֹּאמֶר קַיִן אֶל־יְהֹוָה גָּדוֹל עֲוֺנִי מִנְּשֹׂא׃
verse.en: Cain said to GOD, “My punishment is too great to bear!

messages.text: The Torah describes each of these three cardinal sins with the word “great” in the singular, whereas malicious speech is described with the plural term “great things,” indicating that it is equivalent to all three of the other transgressions together.

notes.he: דבהני לא כתיב אלא גדולה והכא [כתיב] גדולות:
notes.en: Increases sins corresponding to three transgressions: for of those only “great” is written, and here “great things” is written.

messages.text: Granted that with regard to malicious speech the verse uses the plural: “Great things,” but the plural indicates a minimum of two. If so, one can only say that malicious speech is equivalent to two of the cardinal transgressions.
Which of them could be taken out as less than the other two? All three are equal. Therefore malicious speech must be equivalent to all three.

notes.he: הא בכולהו כתיב גדולות הלכך כולהו אתו:
notes.en: Which of them would be taken out: “great” is written of all of them, so all of them are included.

notes.he: [כנגד ב' עבירות] דגדולות לא משמע אלא תרי [הי מנייהו מפקת בכולהו כתיב גדולה]:
notes.en: But say two: [corresponding to two transgressions], for “great things” implies only two. [Which of them would you take out? Of all of them “great” is written.]

messages.caption: “Great” is said of each cardinal sin; “great things” is said of the tongue, and none of the three can be left out.

messages.text: Third speech, i.e., malicious speech about a third party, kills three people. It kills the one who speaks malicious speech, and the one who accepts the malicious speech when he hears it, and the one about whom the malicious speech is said.

notes.he: זה לשון הרכיל שהיא שלישית בין אדם לחבירו לגלות לו סוד:
notes.en: Third speech: this is the speech of the talebearer, who is a third between a person and his fellow, revealing a secret to him.

notes.he: לרכיל עצמו שמתוך מריבה שנופלת בין השנים הורגין זה את זה והורגין גואלי הדם את הרכיל שההרג בא על ידו:
notes.en: The one who speaks it: the talebearer himself; for out of the quarrel that falls between the two, they kill each other, and the blood redeemers kill the talebearer, since the killing came about through him.

notes.he: פרש"י לשון שלישי של רכיל מגלה סוד ואני מצאתי כתוב לישנא תליתאי שהקיפה הקב"ה אחת של עצם ואחת של בשר והוא שלישי בתוכם:
notes.en: Third speech: Rashi explains: the third speech, that of the talebearer who reveals a secret. And I found it written: “third tongue,” because the Holy One, Blessed be He, surrounded it with two walls, one of bone and one of flesh, and it is the third, within them.

notes.he: שהאומר שמעו מאחד ואמרו לאחד דהוו ג' בני אדם:
notes.en: Third speech: for the one who speaks heard it from one person and told it to another, so that there are three people.

messages.text: What is the meaning of that which is written: “Death and life are in the hand of the tongue”? Does the tongue have a hand? Rather the verse comes to tell you that just as a hand can kill, so too a tongue can kill.

verse.he: מָוֶת וְחַיִּים בְּיַד־לָשׁוֹן וְאֹהֲבֶיהָ יֹאכַל פִּרְיָהּ׃
verse.en:
Death and life are in the power of the tongue;
Those who love it will eat its fruit.

messages.text: If you were to claim that just as the hand kills only from close by, so too the tongue kills only from close by, therefore the verse states: “Their tongue is a sharpened arrow.” The tongue kills like an arrow that is fired from a bow, at a great distance.

verse.he: חֵץ (שוחט) [שָׁחוּט] לְשׁוֹנָם מִרְמָה דִבֵּר בְּפִיו שָׁלוֹם אֶת־רֵעֵהוּ יְדַבֵּר וּבְקִרְבּוֹ יָשִׂים אׇרְבּוֹ׃
verse.en:
Their tongue is a sharpened arrow,
They use their mouths to deceive.
They speak to their fellows in friendship,
But lay an ambush for them in their hearts.

notes.he: למקום שמגיע אגריפו:
notes.en: From close by: [only] as far as his fist reaches.

messages.text: If you say that just as an arrow can kill only within the distance it can be shot, which is up to about forty or fifty cubits, so too a tongue can kill only from up to forty or fifty cubits, therefore the verse teaches: “They have set their mouth against the heavens, and their tongue walks through the earth.” This teaches that malicious speech can reach great distances, even the distance between heaven and earth.

verse.he: שַׁתּוּ בַשָּׁמַיִם פִּיהֶם וּלְשׁוֹנָם תִּהֲלַךְ בָּאָרֶץ׃
verse.en:
They set their mouths against heaven,
and their tongues range over the earth.

notes.he: דעד סוף העולם יכול להרוג בלשון הרע]:
notes.en: [“They have set their mouth against the heavens”: for one can kill with malicious speech as far as the end of the world.]

messages.text: But since it is written: “They have set their mouth against the heavens, and their tongue walks through the earth,” which teaches that malicious speech reaches between heaven and earth, why do I need that which we derived from the verse: “Their tongue is a sharpened arrow,” i.e., that a tongue can kill from the distance an arrow flies?
This teaches us that a tongue kills in the same manner that an arrow kills.
But since it is written: “Their tongue is a sharpened arrow,” why do I need the verse: “Death and life are in the hand of the tongue,” which merely teaches that a tongue can kill?
This verse is necessary for a statement of Rava,

One who wants life can attain it by means of his tongue, which he can use for speaking appropriately and studying Torah. One who wants death can also attain it by means of his tongue, by using it for inappropriate and malicious speech.

notes.he: יעסוק בדברי שטות ונבלה:
notes.en: One who wants death, by his tongue: let him engage in words of folly and obscenity.

notes.he: יעסוק בתורה:
notes.en: One who wants life, by his tongue: let him engage in Torah.

notes.he: [דבעי חיי בלישניה שעוסק בתורה:
notes.en: [One who wants life, by his tongue: that he engages in Torah.]

messages.text: What is considered malicious speech? In other words, how is malicious speech defined and what are the limits of the prohibition?
For example, if one says: There is always fire at so-and-so’s home, indicating that they are always cooking food there.

notes.he: דמשמע עשיר הוא וכל שעה מצוי אש בביתו לבשל תבשילין:
notes.en: Fire at so-and-so’s home: implying that he is rich, and fire is always to be found in his house for cooking dishes.

notes.he: כששואלין ב"א איכן נקח אש והוא אומר יש בביתו של פלוני שמתקנין שם כל היום מאכל:
notes.en: Who says, “There is fire at so-and-so’s home”: when people ask, “Where can we get fire?”, and he says, “There is some at so-and-so’s house, where they prepare food all day.”

messages.text: @Rava What did this person do wrong by saying that there is always fire in that home? His statement is merely revealing the true facts, and is not malicious speech. Rather, it is considered malicious speech if he expressed this in a slanderous manner. For example, if he says: Where else can one find fire except at so-and-so’s home, because they are always cooking food there.
messages.quote: There is always fire at so-and-so’s home

notes.he: הואיל ואינו אומרה בלשון הרע אלא מגלה לאותן שמבקשין אור לכו לבית פלוני:
notes.en: It is merely revealing a matter: since he does not say it as malicious speech, but tells those who are looking for fire: go to so-and-so’s house.

messages.text: Any statement that is said in the presence of its master, i.e., if the subject of the statement was there, does not have any prohibition due to malicious speech.

notes.he: שהמרגל אומרה בפני האומר עליו:
notes.en: That is said in the presence of its master: that the talebearer says it in the presence of the one he is speaking about.

messages.text: All the more so it is proscribed speech, as it is both impudence and malicious speech.
messages.quote: said in the presence of its master

messages.text: I hold in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yosei,
In all my days I never said something and then turned around to see if the person I was speaking about was standing behind me listening, as I would say it even to the person involved.

notes.he: לראות מי יעמוד אחורי שאף בפני הבעלים אני אומרה אלמא לאו לישנא בישא חשיבא. ל"א שאם באו הבעלים ואמרו למה אמרת כן לא חזרתי בי לאמר לא אמרתי אלא בפניהם הודיתי:
notes.en: And turned around behind me: to see who might be standing behind me, for I would say it even in the presence of the people concerned; evidently, it is not considered malicious speech. Another version: if the people concerned came and asked, “Why did you say this?”, I never went back on it and said “I did not say it”; rather I admitted it to their faces.

notes.dh: מעולם לא אמרתי דבר שחזרתי לאחורי
notes.he: כלומר כשהייתי אומר דבר על שום אדם לא צרכתי לחזור לאחורי ולראות שלא יהא שם בעל הדבר שאפי' אם יהיה שם לא היה חושש שאינו משקר ואין אומרו בלשון הרע:
notes.en: I never said a thing and then turned around: that is, when I would say something about anyone, I did not need to turn around and look to see that the person concerned was not there; for even if he were there, I would not worry, since I do not lie and do not say it as malicious speech.

messages.text: The daf breaks off as the next teaching begins: “says…” It continues on 16a, where Rabba bar Rav Huna says that a matter said in the presence of three people is not malicious speech, because your friend has a friend, and your friend’s friend has a friend.
